findings.title: Public member list silently capped at 50 with no paging UI
findings.body: The members action now applies a default limit of 50 to every group. Previously non-automatic groups returned all members. The public members route (group-members.js.es6) calls findMembers() once with the defaults, and the template group/members.hbs has no next/previous controls. In any group with more than 50 members, the public page shows only the first 50 and gives users no way to reach the rest. Either add paging to the public page or keep returning the full list there.

findings.title: GET /groups/:name/members.json response shape changed from array to object
findings.body: The endpoint used to return a bare JSON array of serialized members. It now returns {members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}. Any existing consumer that treats the response as an array (API clients, plugins, other frontend code) will break. The change is not versioned or called out, and only the consumers in this PR were updated.

findings.title: Negative limit or offset causes a database error (500)
findings.body: limit and offset come straight from params through to_i with no validation. A negative value (for example offset=-1) is passed into LIMIT/OFFSET, which PostgreSQL rejects, so the request returns a 500 instead of a client error. Previously only automatic groups reached this code path with user-supplied limit/offset; now every group's member endpoint does.

findings.title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. With 100 members and limit 50 this yields 3 pages, not 2. Page 2 shows Next as enabled, and clicking it requests offset 100, which returns an empty page labelled 3/3. Math.ceil(user_count / limit) gives the correct count for all values.

findings.title: create ignores alias_level, which the admin UI sends for new groups
findings.body: The admin form shows the alias_level combo box for new groups too, and Group#asJSON sends alias_level on POST. create only reads name and visible, so the chosen alias level is silently dropped and the group is created with the default. The save action does not call save() again after create, so the value is never persisted. The spec suite has no create test that checks alias_level.

findings.title: PATCH incremental membership API removed; PATCH now silently succeeds without changes
findings.body: The old update_patch handled PATCH with a changes payload (add/delete usernames). That branch is removed, but resources :groups still routes PATCH to update. update now ignores the changes key, saves name/visible/alias_level, and returns success. Existing API clients get HTTP 200 and no membership change, which is a silent no-op instead of an error. Either keep the behaviour or reject PATCH explicitly.

findings.title: Removing a non-member raises RecordNotFound instead of succeeding
findings.body: group.users.delete(user_id) is called with an integer id. In Rails 4.x, CollectionProxy#delete with ids first calls find on the association, so a user who is not in the group raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound and returns a 404. The removed spec explicitly tested that removing non-members succeeds silently, and the admin JS removeMember has no error handler, so a stale list just fails with no feedback.

findings.title: remove_member spec sends PUT although the route is DELETE
findings.body: The route for remove_member is delete "members" in config/routes.rb, but this spec issues xhr :put. Controller specs do not check the HTTP verb against the routes, so the test passes regardless of which verb is mapped. It should use :delete so it exercises the real endpoint.

findings.title: Behaviour changes are untested: pagination endpoint, unknown usernames, non-members, alias_level on create
findings.body: The PR changes the public members endpoint (paginated, new response shape) but adds no test for it in the groups controller spec. It also removes the specs for adding unknown users and removing non-members without replacing them. There is no create test covering alias_level, which is why the dropped value above goes unnoticed. The JS pagination arithmetic (totalPages) has no test either.

findings.title: Remove control shown for automatic groups because the template checks the wrong object
findings.body: This template is rendered once per member, so its context is the member User object. {{#unless automatic}} therefore looks up automatic on the user, which is undefined, and the remove link renders for every member, including automatic groups. Clicking it sends a DELETE that the server rejects with a 422, and the UI has no error handler, so nothing visible happens. The flag should be passed in from the group controller.

findings.title: Offset is clamped to a stale user_count, leaving an empty page after removing the last member
findings.body: findMembers clamps the requested offset to the current user_count. removeMember calls findMembers right after the DELETE returns, before user_count has been refreshed. If the last member on the final page is removed, the request uses the old count, so the page is re-fetched at an offset beyond the new total. The result is an empty table with currentPage past the last page, and the offset is never pulled back to the new last page.

findings.title: Overlapping findMembers responses can leave a stale page displayed
findings.body: Each findMembers call writes members, offset and user_count from its own response. When next or previous is clicked quickly, two requests can be in flight and responses can arrive out of order. The last response to arrive wins, which can be the older page, and nothing discards stale responses. The displayed page and the pager state can then disagree with what the user last requested.

findings.title: Selector for the old user-selector id no longer matches
findings.body: The user-selector input was renamed from id group-users to user-selector in group.hbs, but this rule still targets input#group-users, so its width no longer applies. The enclosing .row.groups rule is also unused now. The selector should be updated or removed.
